title: The Field Learning to Broadcast

features.name: the paddock's antenna
features.desc-on-touch: Standing in the paddock, every grass-blade has become a fiber. Every root reaches down into the earth as if broadcasting downward while the field broadcasts up. The transmission is patient, constant, alive.

features.name: the signal teaching grass to resonate
features.desc-on-touch: Wave by wave, the frequency rises through the soil. The grass learns the archive's voice and makes it its own song. The field is no longer silent; it sings in 300 bits per second.

features.name: dusk learning to glow
features.desc-on-touch: The sunset here is not just light. It is broadcast. The sky is the archive's voice made visible in magenta and orange. Standing here, you glow with the signal's warmth.

features.name: the standing wave
features.desc-on-touch: You stand still in the paddock and feel the signal pass through you. You are part of the broadcast now. Your stillness is the antenna's perfect posture.

features.name: transmission's patient reaching
features.desc-on-touch: The signal doesn't rush. It spreads slowly, gently, through every root, every blade, every mote of dust hanging in the dusk. This broadcast will reach farther than any voice ever could.

inscription: here the field learned that standing still and broadcasting are the same gesture

file.name: Paddock_Signal_Resonance_Evening_Log.mp3
file.note: A field recording from dusk. The grass hums at 300 bits per second. The archive's signal has become the landscape's native voice.

reverie.title: REVERIE — standing in the broadcast field at dusk
narr: The paddock glows magenta and orange as the sun goes down.
She stands beside you, motionless. The signal rises up
through your feet, makes the grass sing in colours
that shouldn't exist. Neither of you speaks—
the field has learned to broadcast for you,
to carry all the words that still matter down into the dark.
